nodes.label: api service (FastAPI backend)
nodes.rationale: Runs 'alembic upgrade head && uvicorn app.main:app' on start; publishes ${API_PORT:-8001}:8000; healthcheck curls /healthz.

nodes.label: scanner service (ARQ worker)
nodes.rationale: network_mode: host with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW gives the worker real L2 access for ARP scanning (Linux only); reaches Postgres/Redis via loopback-published ports; runs 'arq app.worker.worker.WorkerSettings'.

nodes.label: web service (Next.js frontend)
nodes.rationale: Publishes ${WEB_PORT:-3010}:3000; empty NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL means same-origin API access via Next rewrite proxy to the api service.

nodes.label: BACKUP_DIR env var
nodes.rationale: The volume lives and dies with the host — files must be copied off-server for real disaster recovery.

nodes.label: IPAMBOX_ALLOW_INSECURE env var
nodes.rationale: Bypasses roles entirely (trusted-proxy mode) — every request gets full permissions; only for use behind a trusted proxy.

nodes.label: IPAMBOX_PASSWORD[_FILE] env var
nodes.rationale: Prefer IPAMBOX_PASSWORD_FILE (e.g. a Docker secret) so the admin password never sits in env/compose files.

nodes.label: GET/PATCH /api/v1/settings
nodes.rationale: PATCH with {"key": null} resets a key to its env value; PATCH is admin only.

nodes.label: PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}
nodes.rationale: Sessions die with the user; admin only.

nodes.label: Page /prefixes/[id] (subnet matrix, IP table, bulk ops, CSV)
nodes.norm_label: page /prefixes/[id] (subnet matrix, ip table, bulk ops, csv)

nodes.label: Service: api (FastAPI async, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic, Pydantic 2 — host port 8001)
nodes.norm_label: service: api (fastapi async, sqlalchemy 2.0, alembic, pydantic 2 — host port 8001)

nodes.label: Service: db (PostgreSQL 16, btree_gist — 127.0.0.1:5432)
nodes.rationale: Bound to 127.0.0.1 so the database is not exposed to the LAN; btree_gist enables CIDR exclusion constraints.

nodes.label: Service: redis (Redis 7 — ARQ queue, sessions, scan-progress pub/sub — 127.0.0.1:6379)
nodes.norm_label: service: redis (redis 7 — arq queue, sessions, scan-progress pub/sub — 127.0.0.1:6379)
nodes.rationale: Loopback-only for security; carries ARQ jobs, login sessions and live scan-progress pub/sub.

nodes.label: Service: scanner (ARQ worker — Scapy ARP, ICMP ping socket, TCP probes)
nodes.norm_label: service: scanner (arq worker — scapy arp, icmp ping socket, tcp probes)
nodes.rationale: Runs with network_mode: host plus NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW for real L2 ARP access — Linux only because host networking does not exist on Docker Desktop. Reaches Postgres/Redis via loopback-published ports.

nodes.label: Service: web (Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind, TanStack, Recharts — host port 3010)
nodes.norm_label: service: web (next.js 15, react 19, tailwind, tanstack, recharts — host port 3010)

nodes.label: users table
nodes.rationale: Deliberately excluded from backups and never touched by restore — the admin account always belongs to the server you are restoring on.

nodes.label: alembic upgrade head on api start
nodes.norm_label: alembic upgrade head on api start
nodes.rationale: The api command runs 'alembic upgrade head' before uvicorn so the database schema always matches the running code — the same Alembic revision chain that backup files record for restore gating.

nodes.label: BACKUP_DIR env (default /backups)
nodes.rationale: Points api and scanner at the directory where scheduled snapshots are written/listed; defaults to /backups which is exactly where the backupdata volume is mounted.

nodes.label: BACKUP_INTERVAL_MINUTES env (default 0)
nodes.rationale: Recurring backup interval in minutes on both api and scanner; 0 disables scheduling (manual backups only).

nodes.label: BACKUP_KEEP env (default 14)
nodes.rationale: Retention count for scheduled snapshot files, bounding disk use of the backupdata volume.

nodes.label: backupdata volume
nodes.rationale: Named docker volume mounted at /backups on both api and scanner so the worker can write scheduled snapshots and the API can list/serve them; it lives and dies with the host, so files must be copied off-server for real disaster recovery.

nodes.label: backend/app/services/backup.py (BACKUP_TABLES registry — one entry per table ordered by FK dependency)
nodes.norm_label: backend/app/services/backup.py (backup_tables registry — one entry per table ordered by fk dependency)

nodes.label: SECURITY.md (threat model, deployment hardening, vulnerability reporting)
nodes.norm_label: security.md (threat model, deployment hardening, vulnerability reporting)

nodes.label: SCAN_INTERVAL_MINUTES
nodes.rationale: 0 means manual-only scans; recurring schedule applies to the worker within a minute, no restart.

nodes.label: SCAN_INTERVAL_MINUTES env (default 0)
nodes.rationale: Recurring scan interval on api (validation/rate-limit) and scanner (worker execution); the direct analogue of BACKUP_INTERVAL_MINUTES for scan scheduling.

nodes.label: BACKUP_TABLES registry (backend/app/services/backup.py)
nodes.rationale: One registry entry per backed-up table ordered by FK dependency; a test fails if a new table is forgotten.

nodes.label: IPAMBOX_ALLOW_INSECURE
nodes.rationale: Disables auth entirely — documented as only acceptable behind a trusted proxy.

nodes.label: IPAMBOX_PASSWORD[_FILE]
nodes.rationale: Prefer the _FILE variant (e.g. a Docker secret) so the password never sits in env or compose files.

nodes.label: SCAN_EXCLUDE_NETWORKS
nodes.rationale: Hard denylist — these CIDRs may never be scanned regardless of other settings.
